title: Allow users to zoom to at least 500 percent
summary: The viewport meta tag caps zoom with a low maximum-scale. Remove the limit, or raise it, so users can enlarge text further.
problem: The <meta name="viewport"> tag sets a maximum-scale that limits how far users can zoom. Zooming is still possible but stops early, before some people have enlarged the text enough to read it.
whoItAffects: People with low vision who need strong magnification on a phone or tablet. A limit that lets a little zoom through helps some users and still stops those who need more.
steps: Find the <meta name="viewport"> tag in your page template or theme header.
Remove maximum-scale altogether. That is the best option.
If you must keep a limit, raise it to at least 5.
Check on a phone that pinch zoom continues to work and that content stays readable when enlarged.

whyItMatters: This is a best practice, not a WCAG failure. Stronger zoom limits are not required for compliance, but removing the cap costs nothing and helps visitors who need more magnification than the minimum.
howToCheck: View the page source and read the viewport tag. There should be no maximum-scale, or it should be 5 or higher. On a phone, try zooming in as far as the browser allows.
